# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Member Rights and Appeals
Blue Cross and Blue Shield of North Carolina
PO Box 30055
Durham, NC 27702-3055
Fax: 919-765-4409

**From:** Harper Delgado
Member ID: W927303466
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-13 — Reference number POC-332858B095-32885**
**Requested service:** Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446
**Governing policy:** Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/joint-surgery-2025-11-15/

---

Dear Member Rights and Appeals:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). The notice dated 2026-08-13 states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision, because the records already in my file line up with the plan's own published criteria under Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1). My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I take the plan's criteria one at a time and point to where each one is met in my records.

## 1. The imaging requirement

The policy states:

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods: X-ray report or provider interpretation of x-rays that utilizes or can be correlated with the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system of osteoarthritis MRI report from a radiologist that utilizes or can be correlated with the modified Outerbridge or similar classification system related to articular cartilage injury and osteoarthritis"

My records contain an MRI of the knee dated 2026-06-02 — well within the past 12 months — reporting full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially. That is imaging that describes the degree of cartilage damage using the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system, which is exactly what this criterion asks for.

The policy also states:

> "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis, or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

My MRI report describes bone-on-bone apposition and full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment, which speaks directly to the bone-on-bone articulation element of this criterion.

And the policy states:

> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III – IV or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4, isolated to the medial or lateral knee compartment with no degenerative changes in the opposite compartment"

My imaging documents Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially, which falls squarely inside the grade 3 – 4 range the plan itself has set, and the finding is reported in the medial compartment. If the plan's concern is about a specific element of this criterion — for example, findings in the opposite compartment — I ask that the plan say so in writing, identify the criterion it applied and the specific finding it considered missing, and request the complete MRI report and images from Dr. Reyes's office before finalizing its decision. My surgeon and I are ready to supply anything further the reviewer needs.

Finally, the policy states:

> "For x-ray interpretation, the provider shall submit a detailed imaging description that correlates with clinical findings of the requested procedure. In the absence of a detailed description, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

My imaging findings and my clinical findings point the same direction. On examination, I had positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain — findings consistent with the medial cartilage loss and bone-on-bone apposition on the MRI.

## 2. Conservative treatment

The policy states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"

Two things in my record meet this. First, my imaging shows Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially, which is the situation the policy's own parenthetical addresses. Second, even setting that aside, I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-08 to 2026-07-01, with 20 visits completed, documented in my physical therapy discharge note.

The policy states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

I did both. For physical therapy, the policy states:

> "Physical therapy requirement includes ANY of the following: Physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider of physical therapy services Supervised home treatment program that includes ALL the following: Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

My therapy was supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, over 12 weeks and 20 visits, documented in a physical therapy discharge note. That satisfies the first option in this list.

For complementary treatment, the policy states:

> "Complementary conservative treatment requirement includes ANY of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Intra-articular corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

The policy asks for **any one** of these. My records document two: NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and an intra-articular corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-06 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.

The policy states:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

All three are present in my chart. I completed the full course described above for this episode of care. My pain has been progressive over 24 months and is unrelieved by rest, the NSAIDs gave inadequate relief, and the injection relief lasted only 3 weeks — that is not significant improvement. And surgery is now being considered, which is the more invasive therapy this criterion contemplates.

## 3. Documentation of symptoms, function, and reevaluation

The policy states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

My records contain each piece: duration (24 months of progressive pain, unrelieved by rest), specific functional limitations (I cannot climb stairs without assistance, and I wake 3–4 times a night with pain), and the type and duration of every treatment tried (12 weeks and 20 visits of supervised physical therapy from 2026-04-08 to 2026-07-01; NSAIDs for 8 months; a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-06).

The policy states:

> "Reporting symptom severity – Severity of pain and its associated impact on activities of daily living (ADLs) and instrumental ADLs (IADLs) are key factors in determining the need for intervention. For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform ADLs and/or IADLs."

My chart documents that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and that pain wakes me 3–4 times nightly — impairment of ordinary daily activity and of sleep. If the reviewer needs a numeric pain rating recorded on a particular date to complete this element, I ask that the plan request it from Dr. Reyes's office rather than deny on that basis, and I am glad to have it supplied.

The policy states:

> "Clinical reevaluation – In most cases, reevaluation should include a physical examination. Direct contact by other methods, such as telephone communication or electronic messaging, may substitute for in-person evaluation when circumstances preclude an office visit. Clinical reevaluation must be done in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service such that the patient's condition would be unlikely to change by the date of service."

I was examined in person, with positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, and my physical therapy course concluded on 2026-07-01 — shortly before the authorization request. My condition has been progressive and has not reversed.

## 4. Other criteria in the policy

The policy also states:

> "Intact anterior cruciate ligament or documentation of stable knee examination (UKA may done with concurrent ACL reconstruction if all other criteria are met)"

and

> "Where there are patient specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient, a shared decision-making process to discuss these modifiable comorbidities with the patient is strongly recommended and should be documented."

On the second point, my record documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker. On the ligament and alignment criteria — the policy also states "Less than 10 degrees of fixed varus deformity for medial UKA" and "Less than 15 degrees of fixed valgus deformity for lateral UKA" — my records as summarized to me do not report those specific measurements one way or the other, and I am not going to characterize findings my chart does not state. Dr. Reyes's office can provide the operative planning and examination details on these points on request, and I ask that the plan request them.

I should also note plainly that I have only a set of excerpts from Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1), not the complete guideline. The policy contains further conditions that were not reproduced for me. I am not quoting or characterizing any plan language beyond the excerpts above, and I ask the plan to identify in writing exactly which criterion or criteria it applied in reaching the 2026-08-13 determination.

## What I am asking for

I am asking the plan to overturn the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 and approve the procedure. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask that it provide, in writing:

1. the specific criterion from Carelon Joint Surgery (MSK02-1125.1) that my imaging was found not to meet, and the specific imaging finding the reviewer considered missing;
2. the complete criteria set the reviewer applied; and
3. the credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

I also ask that Dr. Reyes be given the opportunity to discuss this case with the reviewing physician, and that the plan request my full MRI report, physical therapy discharge note, and office notes directly from his office if they are not already in the file.

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, which the notice states is by **2027-02-09**. I am submitting this letter to Member Rights and Appeals at the mailing address and fax number above, and I am attaching a Member Appeal Form. I can also be reached through the phone number on the back of my insurance card if anything further is needed.

Thank you for taking a careful second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Harper Delgado**
Member ID: W927303466
Reference number: POC-332858B095-32885
